title: Regulations and Brain Drain: Evidence from Wall Street Star Analysts' Career Choices
eligible_reason: Single reform period (post-reform 2004-2007 vs pre-reform 1995-2001) applied to all analysts, estimated with logistic regression. STAR x D is a group-by-post interaction, not staggered adoption. Nonlinear model and time-varying controls.
design_notes: Eq. (1): logit of LeftSell-Side on D (post-reform), STAR, D x STAR, and controls (NFIRM, SANCTIONED, LOGFEE, SENTIMENT, forecast accuracy, experience etc.). Table 4 reports logistic regressions (some with sanctioned-bank effects). Reforms (Global Settlement, SOX 501, NASD/NYSE rules) became effective 2002-2003 and the years 2002-2003 are dropped (robustness includes them in post). No unit FE, no calendar-time FE. Published in MS 65(12):5766-5784.
estimators_reported: logit with D x STAR interaction

ineligible_specs.reason: logistic model; single reform date; time-varying controls; no unit or time FE
same single-date group-by-post structure with controls

screener_notes: Data are I/B/E/S (Thomson), Institutional Investor All-America Research Team lists and SDC underwriting data (all licensed), plus analyst career-destination data (Table 7).
